findings.title: plural_noun crashes with IndexError on title-cased 'X Of A Y' compounds
findings.property: plural_noun never raises on a valid non-empty word/phrase, including when the phrase is capitalised
findings.expected: 'Sons Of Guns' (lowercase 'son of a gun' gives 'sons of guns')
findings.actual: IndexError: list index out of range in engine.postprocess (inflect/__init__.py:2376)
findings.evidence: plural_noun accepts any Word; lowercase 'son of a gun' -> 'sons of guns' is tested in tests/test_pwd.py. The dual-compound branch of _plnoun drops the 'a', so the result has fewer words than the input, and postprocess's per-word capitalisation loop indexes result[index] for each original word, which overruns when the original word 'A' is capitalised.

review.title: plural_noun raises IndexError on title-cased 'Son Of A Gun' because postprocess indexes past a shorter result
review.reason: The lowercase 'son of a gun' works and is tested, giving 'sons of guns', and 'Son Of A Gun' is an ordinary non-empty phrase, so it is a valid input. The dual-compound branch drops the 'a', so `result` has 3 words while `orig` has 4. `postprocess`'s capitalisation loop indexes `result[index]` by the original word count and overruns on the last word, which I reproduced as an IndexError at `inflect/__init__.py:2376`. The loop is meant to carry capitalisation over to the result, so it should be bounds-safe. A maintainer would accept a fix such as guarding the index or aligning words.

findings.reproSource:
import inflect


def test_repro_title_case_dual_compound():
    p = inflect.engine()
    assert p.plural_noun("son of a gun") == "sons of guns"
    # Capitalised version of the same phrase must not crash
    assert p.plural_noun("Son Of A Gun") == "Sons Of Guns"
